# czc-v2026.10.29.1 (0.2.19.2)

Gateway fixes for Codex clients. Requests no longer fail with
`websocket upgrade failed: status 403` when chatgpt.com rejects the upstream
WebSocket handshake, and multi-turn Codex conversations that used web search
no longer fail on the next turn.

## Changes since czc-v2026.10.28.2

### Gateway: upstream WebSocket handshake 403

Clients (Codex CLI / Codex VS Code) intermittently got
`unexpected status 403 Forbidden: websocket upgrade failed: status 403`.
The 403 came from chatgpt.com rejecting the gateway's upstream WebSocket
handshake. The same accounts kept serving other requests in the same minute,
which points at edge (Cloudflare) blocks on the egress rather than account
bans. On 2026-10-29 between 03:00 and 04:00 UTC about 210 requests failed
this way.

The gateway treated that 403 like a credential failure: no retry, no HTTP
fallback, no account switch. Now:

- HTTP `/responses` requests retry the same request over HTTP on the same
  account. The session is not pinned to HTTP. If HTTP also returns 403, the
  existing OpenAI 403 rules apply (edge pages are not counted against the
  account, structured 403s cool down the account and switch).
- Client WebSocket sessions (first turn) and v2 passthrough sessions switch
  to another account. Only a structured JSON 403 counts against the account;
  HTML, empty, plain-text or `cf-mitigated` responses do not.
- A 401 on the handshake keeps the old behavior (token refresh, no fallback).
- Failed requests now include a `ws_dial_rejected` entry in the ops error
  log's upstream attempts, with `server`, `cf-ray`, `cf-mitigated`,
  `content-type` and up to 1 KB of the response body, labelled
  `edge_forbidden` or `account_forbidden`.

### Gateway: web search history without an id

Multi-turn Codex conversations that used web search failed on later turns
with `gateway web search history without an id is unavailable or expired`.
Codex keeps only `type`/`query`/`queries` of `web_search_call.action`, so the
gateway's fingerprint (which included `action.sources`) never matched the
replayed item.

- The fingerprint now uses only fields that survive the round trip.
- Hosted search mode: unmatched id-less history (expired, restart, other
  scope, ambiguous, failed search) becomes a neutral assistant note restating
  the client's own query instead of a 400. Search results are never guessed.
- Non-hosted mode: unmatched id-less items pass through unchanged, and
  unchanged request bodies are not re-encoded.

### Deploy assets

- `deploy/devin-tool-sanitize/proxy.py`: rewrites OpenClaw's
  `a personal assistant running inside` opener (blocked by Devin swe-2 as
  content policy), strips Claude Code's one-turn system nudge so the cached
  prefix stays stable, and drops `temperature: 0` (rejected by Devin). The
  repository copy now matches the copy already installed on the server; this
  release does not change the running sanitize proxy.

## VERSION

`0.2.19.2`

## Upgrade guidance

- No database migration. No configuration change.
- API key auth cache snapshot version is unchanged.
- Replace the binary and restart `sub2api.service`.

## Compatibility

- Requests that used to fail with a handshake 403 now succeed over HTTP or
  on another account. They can be slightly slower (one failed WebSocket
  handshake before the retry).
- No API or response format changes.

## Verification

Passed:

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go vet -tags unit ./internal/...`,
  `gofmt`.
- `go test -count=1 -tags unit ./...`: all 61 packages pass.
- `go test -count=1 ./...`: all packages pass.
- New tests: handshake 403 classification, edge vs account 403 detection,
  ops evidence recording, no account penalty for edge 403s, cooldown for
  structured 403s, and an end-to-end forward test where a Cloudflare-style
  403 handshake falls back to HTTP. The forward test fails with the old
  classification.
- `proxy.py` parses (`ast.parse`) and is identical to the installed copy.
- Frontend `vue-tsc -b` and `vite build` for the embedded admin UI.

Failed or skipped:

- golangci-lint was not run (not installed on the build host).
- `-tags=integration` and `-tags=e2e` suites were not run; no repository or
  migration code changed.
- Frontend unit tests were not run; no frontend code changed.
- The handshake 403 fallback was not tested against a live Cloudflare block
  before deploy; it is checked after deploy through the ops error log.

## Rollback

Redeploy `czc-v2026.10.28.2`, or restore the backup
`/opt/sub2api/sub2api.bak.czc-v2026.10.29.1-<UTC timestamp>` created during
this deploy and restart `sub2api.service`. There is no migration, so no
database rollback is needed.
